memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'The assembly must protect the one accused of murder from the avenger of blood and send the accused back to the city of refuge to which they fled. The accused must stay there until the death of the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil. But if the accused ever goes outside the limits of the city of refuge and the avenger of blood finds them outside the city, the avenger of blood may kill the accused without being guilty of murder. The accused must stay in the city of refuge until the death of the high priest; only after the death of the high priest may they return to their own property.'" - Num 35:25-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
There is a fascinating detail here. The one who had fled to the city of refuge had to remain there until the death of the high priest. Only then could they return home freely. Their freedom was tied to the death of the high priest — as if the priest's death released them from their confinement and restored them to their inheritance. Until then, safety was found only within the city.

This is one of the most striking pictures of Christ in the whole Old Testament. The person's release and restoration came through the death of the high priest. And we have a great High Priest, Jesus Christ, whose death sets us free. It is through the death of our High Priest that we are released from the confinement of sin and restored to our true inheritance (Heb 9:15). What the death of Israel's high priest did in shadow, the death of Jesus accomplished in full and forever.

Notice too that safety was found only by staying within the city. To step outside was to expose oneself to danger. Likewise, our safety is found only in remaining in Christ. Jesus said, "Remain in me, and I will remain in you" (John 15:4). We are secure as we abide in Him, sheltered in our Refuge.

But here is the glory of the gospel over the shadow: the person in the city waited for a priest to die who would eventually die of natural causes, and then their old life resumed. Our High Priest died once for sin, rose again, and lives forever. His death has permanently freed us, and His endless life keeps us secure. We do not wait anxiously in refuge; we rest joyfully in a finished redemption.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does it move you that the high priest's death pictures Christ's death setting you free?
2. What does it mean for you to "remain" in Christ, your Refuge?
3. How does Jesus' unending life give you lasting security?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, my great High Priest, thank You that Your death has set me free and restored my inheritance. Help me to remain in You, my Refuge, resting in the finished redemption and endless life You give. Amen.
